title: appbuilder-mvp cannot pass its own hard gates (stories.yaml, 07_screens)
detail: `spec-featuresets` hard-gates `_concept/04_journeys/stories.yaml`, but the flow has no `experience-journeys` node. `build-plan` and `build-implement` hard-gate `_concept/07_screens`, but the flow has no `spec-feature` or `experience-shell` node. Three hard gates in this flow have no upstream writer.
recommendation: Add the producing nodes to `appbuilder-mvp`, or make the three gates `soft` and say in each step what changes without the file. Add the check.py rule of F04.

title: appbuilder-standard runs mockup-storybook before the tech stack it hard-gates on
detail: `mockup-storybook` hard-gates `10_blueprint/techstack.md` and reads it in step 1. In `appbuilder-standard` it runs at node 12; `architecture-techstack` runs at node 15, after annotate and feedback. The gate cannot be open when the node starts.
recommendation: Move `architecture-techstack` and `architecture-system` before the mockup nodes. Or gate `mockup-storybook` soft and take the framework from the template default.

title: skaileup-concept-reverse runs spec-feature; nothing writes its scope.yaml gate
detail: `spec-feature` hard-gates `_concept/01_meta/scope.yaml`. The reverse flow starts at `concept-reverse`, which only reads that file, and has no `concept-scope` node. When the host's profile picker starts the flow, no node writes `scope.yaml`. A grep of `skaile-forge/server` for `scope.yaml` and `01_meta` finds 0 hits, so the host writes none either.

evidence.quote: started the run from an onboarding profile

recommendation: Make `concept-scope` the entry of the reverse flow, or let `concept-reverse` write `scope.yaml` with `flow: skaileup-concept-reverse`.

title: check.py never checks that a hard gate has an upstream writer
detail: The docstring says a prerequisite no skill writes is raised here. `_check_one_flow` (lines 730-842) checks id, name, presentation, node ids, edge types, reachability and `requires:`. It never compares a node's hard gate with the nodes upstream, so F01 to F03 stay green. A search of check.py for writer or producer logic finds none.

evidence.quote: prerequisite path that no skill writes is a gate that can never open

recommendation: Add a rule: walk each flow's `type: flow` edges, collect the targets written so far, and fail on a hard gate with no writer upstream. It needs the `produces` list of F05.

title: No skill declares what it produces, so the editor cannot derive done state
detail: The editor marks a node done from `contracts/artifacts.yaml` `produced_by`, and falls back to the session when none exists. This collection ships no such file: ADR 0001 records it as unreachable under a copy install, and no skill frontmatter has a `produces` key. `skaileup` step 3.2 therefore walks the tree for the first node whose artifacts are missing, with no list to look up.

evidence.quote: Producing skills; the FIRST is the canonical producer.
The first node whose artifacts are not yet in the tree

recommendation: Add `metadata.artifacts.produces: [{id, path}]` to every skill, checked by check.py. Ask the host to read done state from that list, as it already reads `artifacts.requires`.

title: Dialog answers have two homes: host user_input.json and answers.json
detail: The host stores each step's dialog input at `_concept/_grounding/<step>/user_input.json` and injects it into the prompt. The collection keeps answers at `02_grounding/onboarding/answers.json`, and a search of `skaile-forge/server` for `answers.json` finds 0 hits. Only `concept-onboard` mentions `answers.json` among the skills. The other skills' dialog values stay in the host file.

evidence.quote: The host writes its own per-skill dialog file

recommendation: Make `concept-onboard` step 1 merge what the host handed in into `answers.json` once. Record the host path as a fact in `scripts/host_facts.py`.

title: Contract volume: 13 files, 2,373 lines, cited whole
detail: The 13 contracts hold 2,373 lines (README.md and CONTRACT.md excluded). `spec-feature` and `architecture-datamodel` cite 7 contracts each. `experience-shell` cites 4; two of them, `elements_block.md` (401 lines) and `walkthrough_renderer.md` (445 lines), serve one `kind: nav` element in step 6.
recommendation: Cite `§` sections, as the skills already do for `agent_patterns.md`. Point `experience-shell` at `elements_block.md § Schema` and `walkthrough_renderer.md § App-shell navigation`.

title: The domain glossary sits in the blueprint and is written by three skills
detail: The glossary is `10_blueprint/glossary.md`. `concept-brief` writes it at node 3 of 27, `spec-feature` writes it during every feature, and `architecture-datamodel` settles it at node 17. `experience-journeys`, `spec-featuresets`, `experience-behaviors` and `experience-shell` have 0 mentions of `glossary` in their SKILL.md and references.
recommendation: Put one `glossary.md` beside `brief.md`. One step writes it right after the brief; every later skill reads it.

title: concept-reverse is a second writer of six artifacts
detail: `concept-reverse` writes `brief.md`, `goals.md`, `comparable.md`, `10_blueprint/techstack.md`, `03_brand/identity.md` and `03_brand/tokens.json`. Their owners are `concept-brief`, `architecture-techstack` and `design-brand`. The `extraction_confidence` grades appear only in `concept-reverse`, and no owner names it.

evidence.quote: `brief.md` takes the pitch, audience, problem and hero flow

recommendation: Let `concept-reverse` write only `02_grounding/findings/*`. The owning skills read those findings as seeds.

title: Competitor knowledge lives in two files
detail: `concept-research` writes `02_grounding/research/competitors.md`. `concept-brief` writes `comparable.md`, a second file about the same competitor products. No rule says which file is the source.
recommendation: Keep one file. Make `comparable.md` a section of `brief.md` that cites `competitors.md`.

title: Screenshots have three homes
detail: Screenshots go to `02_grounding/findings/`, to `02_grounding/research/step/<skill name>/` or to `03_brand/references/`. Two skills write them, and no rule picks one home.

evidence.quote: Screenshots, page saves and excerpts go under

recommendation: Use `02_grounding/findings/` only, with a `step` field in `findings/index.md`.

title: concept-research is "not a pipeline step" but both flows place it after brief
detail: `concept-research` says it has no place in the order. `appbuilder-standard` and `skaileup-concept-only` run it right after `concept-brief`. `concept-brief` step 1 reads the research files "where research ran first", so in both flows those files do not exist yet.

evidence.quote: It is not a pipeline step with a

recommendation: Run research before brief, or delete the node and keep the "alongside" semantics.

title: Approvals and choices stay in chat
detail: `concept-brief` waits for a "yes in words", and `design-brand` iterates until the user approves; neither records the approval in a file. `artifact_frontmatter.md` has no `approved` field (grep: 0 hits). The monorepo choice in `concept-reverse` and the seed-table corrections in `concept-onboard` are not recorded either. The editor shows the result, never the decision.

evidence.quote: **Show the brief and wait for a yes in words.**
Iterate until they approve in words.
ask which is the app rather than picking the first
Show the table and let the user correct it before recording
ISO date, updated on every write

recommendation: Add `approved: <date>` to the universal frontmatter fields and write it at each approval. Record every dialog answer in `answers.json`.

title: "One question per message" is restated in six skills
detail: Six skills restate the rule in their own words. Five also cite `agent_patterns.md § Questions Are Standalone Messages`; `design-brand` does not.

evidence.quote: Ask each question as its own message per
one question at a time per

recommendation: Let the contract alone carry the rule. A skill lists only which questions it asks.

title: "Unset type is web-app" is stated twice; the flow choice is described twice
detail: `concept-scope` and `concept-onboard` both state that an unset project type reads as `web-app`. `concept-scope` step 4 describes how the flow is chosen, and `skaileup` describes it again and names the host's profile picker as a second chooser.

evidence.quote: a project whose type is unset behaves as `web-app`
**Record the flow, and derive it only when nothing else has.**
belongs to `concept-scope` step 4, and to the host's profile picker before that

recommendation: Give each fact one owner: `concept-scope` owns the `web-app` default and the flow choice, and `skaileup` only points at it.
